beats.purpose: Hook: introduce the hero, the place and the problem.
First branch. Find an item that matters later.
Paths meet. The hero may go back for what was missed.
A choice that is locked without the item or clue, with a hint, plus an open alternative.
The big moment. Choices lead to different endings.
Best ending: earned with clue and item.
Gentle setback ending that invites another try.

notes: Keep sentences at or under 13 words.
Every ending must be reachable; no passage may trap the reader.
Continuity fact: Castellan Hall is an invented old community theater, not a real building
Continuity fact: The storm has knocked out the phone line, and the one front gate locked itself when the power flickered
Continuity fact: Wren Castellan built the theater full of small mechanical tricks: hidden levers, a false shelf, a trick step

Continuity fact: Key recurring nouns and verbs in the story (names, the lock, the key, the chest, the stage, the steps, the gate, the clock, the coin, rush, shut, wish) contain no letter b, d, p or q; short, hard-to-avoid function words like and, had and said may still appear
Avoid: violence, gore or anyone being badly hurt
Avoid: real brands, companies, places or real people
Avoid: any real religion, god or sacred rite
Avoid: no one is trapped underwater or truly in danger of drowning; the risk is cold, wet, and losing time, solved by working the clues, not a fight

Avoid: do not introduce a new recurring character name, object noun or action verb that contains the letter b, d, p or q; if one is unavoidable, keep it to a single one-off mention, never a repeated or tracked word
